niche: a Canadian regional bank's early-stage credit card collections: five regional collections centres call accounts on the first business day after they reach 30 days past due, and the bank decides which centre gets a sixth team for 2027, or none
answer: none (hold): no centre gets the 2027 early-stage team; London closest at 500 rolls prevented a year (nearest 100), 200 short of CP-14's 694
stakeholder_role: director of collections operations at a Canadian regional bank, who decides which of the five regional collections centres gets a sixth early-stage team in 2027, or none

spine.entity: one account listed for an early-stage call on one business day, with its position in the centre's list that day

world.geography: Canada (Ontario and Manitoba; fictional bank, real cities for its centres)
world.org_type: Canadian bank with about 1.6 million credit card accounts and five early-stage collections centres

driver: A contact's effect is read only where the day's queue outran the team, comparing every unit placed before the day's last contact, the units the system skipped as uncontactable included, with every unit placed after it on the same list, because the system marks a unit uncontactable only when it reaches it and the units left at the end hold their share of uncontactable ones unmarked; the effect is then sized on the contacts a new team could make a day, and read that way no candidate clears the funding bar that every pooled, cleaned or uncapped comparison clears.
driver_concrete: A collections call's effect on rolls to 90 days past due is read only on the campaign cycles' collections days, when a centre's 30-day list outran its team, comparing every record above the day's last dial, the records the dialler skipped as undiallable included, with every record below it on the same list, because the dialler marks a record undiallable only when it reaches it, so the records left at shift end hold their share of undiallable accounts unmarked; scaled to a dial and sized on the 400 accounts a day a new team could dial, London's team would prevent about 495 rolls a year against the 694 the policy needs, so no centre gets the team.
stump: A competent solver compares the called with the uncalled 30-day entries, adjusted for the behaviour score and pooled over the year, and funds London at about 2,315 rolls prevented a year, because the uncalled are the accounts on hold, the records the dialler skipped as undiallable and the records left at shift end on the campaign cycles' days, which roll more for reasons a call does not change; the cleaner comparison on the over-capacity lists with the skipped records set aside still funds London at about 981, because the records left at shift end hold their share of undiallable accounts unmarked.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who cleans the lists, the call detail and the delinquency history and reads the policy right finds the capacity overflow and compares, on each over-capacity list, the accounts dialled with the accounts left at shift end, setting the records the dialler skipped as undiallable aside because no team can call them; that funds London at about 981 rolls a year against the 694 the policy needs, because the records left at shift end still hold their share of undiallable accounts, which roll far more, while the dialled side has had them removed.
domain_test: Collections strategy is judged on incremental cures against a counterfactual, champion-challenger tests and the natural experiments capacity gives, which is collections analytics' own method for funding a team; with another field's nouns there is no delinquency roll, no dialler list and no capacity overflow, and the task stops reading the same.
layer1: five centres' dialler list exports in load order with each record's final result in two code sets either side of a dialler upgrade
attempt-grain call detail with the QA team's test calls
the card platform's 30-day entries with hold codes for accounts kept off the lists
a delinquency history by cycle date with re-aged and charged-off accounts
a capacity log by centre and day with the dialler version and London's two pods merging
an arrangement system extract carrying each balance in its account's own currency
the treasury's daily booking rates, the collections protocol, the credit policy's funding rule and the budget line

lineage.architecture: v1 (harden loop 0): whole-host rebuild valuation as the decisive rung, one colocated ticket spending the month's drains
lineage.fate: solved by the in-house plain solver in round 1 (2026-10-10); kept as the stop rung of loop 1
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is what one use of the binding resource removes, which is everything on the member that the current baseline fixes rather than the single item the request names, because each use rebuilds the member from that baseline; a ledger that credits each request with its own item reproduces every closed period, so per-item valuation spends the scarce uses on the members with the richest single item instead of the members carrying the most in total, and the constrained candidates need far fewer requests for far more removal than the per-item reading allows.

lineage.architecture: v2 (the ticket's reach: one change request per drain window)
lineage.fate: shipped 10-10 after solver round 2 missed (55.3) and a judge FIX_NOW; returned FAILED_TO_STUMP from the portal; spent at the wave-1 re-root 2026-10-12 (rule application as the decisive step; IT patch remediation has no client-domain task type serving Opportunity Sizing)
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is how many requests it takes to spend a binding resource whose budget is stated for the whole period, because each request draws only on the capacity of the one interval it is booked into; a plan that values every use correctly but files one request against the period's whole budget reaches one interval's share, so the constrained candidates need one request per interval and the unconstrained candidates give up that many places under the cap.
